clue.text: Again order extremely reliable cutting guide

indicators.note: only the two extreme letters of the word reliable are wanted here

parts.note: a jig is a workshop device that guides a saw or drill

explanation.surface: Praise for a dependable template used when slicing something, oddly prefixed by 'Again order'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange or reorganise something is a synonym of setting it in order a second time.

clue.text: Waif finally wearing a warmer in bad weather

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the word for bad weather

parts.note: rain is the classic bad weather

indicators.note: the final letter of the word wearing is taken

parts.note: a muff is a fur tube that warms the hands

explanation.surface: A street child, at last, is dressed in something warm during a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragged, neglected child is a waif, a synonym for a scruffy urchin.

clue.text: Post book

definitions.meaning: a post is a position of employment
the Book of ... in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An instruction to mail a book, or a postal service for books.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a position of work; the Old Testament has a book named after the patient sufferer.

clue.text: Hail regularly getting inside my shoe

indicators.note: the picked letters go within the exclamation for my

parts.note: my! and gosh! are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: every other letter of the word Hail is taken, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims as hailstones get into their shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber overshoe worn in wet weather, a specific kind of footwear.

clue.text: Cut up about small dalliance, almost moved

indicators.note: the chopped word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to dice is to cut up into cubes

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped, leaving it nearly whole

parts.note: dalliance is amorous play

explanation.surface: Someone upset by a brief fling is nearly emotionally moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shifted from its usual position has been moved, a synonym.

clue.text: Dawn said prying should be punished after one is sacked

indicators.note: punishing the letters means beating them into a new order
being sacked means the letter for one is dismissed from the group

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone said nosiness deserves punishment once a worker has been fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link word; 'one is sacked' removes one I from SAIDPRYING, and 'should be punished' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dayspring is a poetic word for daybreak, the first light of morning.

clue.text: Top cop, one petitioning for retention of power

indicators.note: the petitioner word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a suer is one who sues or petitions
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A senior police officer who is also campaigning to keep their authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for superintendent, a high rank in the British police.

clue.text: Not initially miserable, one not locally a celebrity

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for miserable is removed

parts.note: glum means miserable
I is the Roman numeral one
nary is a dialect word meaning not or not any, so locally signals the regional usage

explanation.surface: A grumpy person, not from these parts, turns out to be famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous or eminent person is figuratively a shining light, a synonym for a star.

clue.text: Vegetable reported as a dog-rose?

indicators.note: reported means as it is spoken, the sound rather than the spelling

parts.note: whimsically, a collie is a dog and a rose is a flower, so a collie flower

explanation.surface: A puzzling question whether a vegetable could be described as a wild rose.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog-rose is a real wild rose, but here it is split: a dog (collie) plus a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassica with a white head of florets, an example of a vegetable.

clue.text: Mysterious river ending in swamp

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales/England

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word swamp is used

explanation.surface: A strange river that finishes in marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deep is profound and hard to fathom, hence obscure or enigmatic.

clue.text: Fail to rise in corporation? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
this reverses the order the clue states, so the stomach goes into the rising phrase instead

parts.note: to go up is to rise
corporation is a jocular old word for a paunch or stomach

explanation.surface: A company failing to grow, phrased as a question.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the clue puts rising into the stomach; 'On the contrary' flips that, so the stomach word goes inside the rising phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a business collapsing, like a dead fish floating upturned.

clue.text: Colour caused by radiation in West?

indicators.note: the radiation letters go inside the name

parts.note: Mae West, the American actress
UV is ultraviolet radiation

explanation.surface: A question whether a colour results from radiation in the western world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a direction, but it is Mae West, the Hollywood star.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale purple shade, named after the mallow flower, an example of a colour.

clue.text: Duo promised an unusual way of working

indicators.note: an unusual version of these letters is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: A pair vowed to adopt an unconventional method.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for method of operating, used for a characteristic manner of doing a job.

clue.text: European style of writing I found in academic account

indicators.note: these pieces lie within the word for academic

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
script is a style of handwriting

explanation.surface: A report about a European handwriting style the narrator found in a scholar's write-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An account of something is a portrayal or report of what it is like, a synonym.

clue.text: Not strict new diet, so take your time

parts.note: easy means lenient or not strict

indicators.note: a new version of these letters is a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Advice that a relaxed new eating plan means no rushing.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom urging care and slowness, the same advice as not hurrying.

clue.text: Fine, sort of, perhaps brill?

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
-ish means sort of, as in greenish

explanation.surface: Someone asks if 'fine, more or less' is what slangy 'brill' means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brill' poses as slang for brilliant; it is a flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is a flatfish related to turbot, an example of the creature, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Pantomime character transgressed in speech before everyone turned

indicators.note: in speech means we want how the word for transgressed is pronounced, not its spelling

parts.note: to have sinned is to have transgressed; said aloud it is one syllable, 'sind'
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: turned means the word for everyone is read backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A panto figure who misbehaved in what they said before the whole cast turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' gives the sound 'sind', spelt CIND; 'turned' reverses ALL to give LLA at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The rags-to-riches heroine of a favourite British Christmas pantomime, an example of a stock character.

clue.text: Old woman entering depression that comes from mister?

definitions.note: a mister is a spray nozzle, so this is what a spray gives out

indicators.note: the old woman goes inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a small depression
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An elderly lady stepping into a hollow, linked to a man called Mister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mister' poses as Mr but is a sprayer: spray deodorant comes from one.
explanation.definitionFit: A product applied to mask body odour, often dispensed from an aerosol spray.

clue.text: Idle talk's left one scrambling around to check opinion

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap round the chatter and the numeral
scrambling these letters jumbles them into a new order

parts.note: yak is slang for chatter or idle talk
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Gossip has deserted someone who is rushing about to test views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts YAKI inside FLTE, the jumble of LEFT from 'scrambling'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for floating an idea to test people's reaction, like testing the water.

clue.text: Incorrigible cold bishop dismissed for organising this?

definitions.text: Incorrigible cold bishop dismissed for organising this?

indicators.note: organising the remaining letters arranges them in a new order
the two letters are thrown out of the long word

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
B is the chess-notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An incorrigibly icy bishop is sacked, maybe for promoting godlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' takes C and B from INCORRIGIBLE; 'organising' rearranges INORRIGILE. The whole clue imagines why a bishop would be fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of faith or hostility to religion, plausibly a sacking offence for a bishop.

clue.text: Viewed from the east, Yr Wyddfa — extremely twisted

indicators.note: in an across clue, viewing from the east means reading from right to left, backwards
the extreme letters, first and last, of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Seen from the eastern side, Snowdon looks very bent.
explanation.walkthrough: Yr Wyddfa is the Welsh name for Snowdon, the highest mountain in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew or crooked is out of true, a synonym of bent out of shape.

clue.text: Singular flower, one causing much joy?

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
the flower of something is its best part, the cream

explanation.surface: A unique bloom that brings great delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom here but the finest part, as in the flower of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A very funny person or thing is informally called this, a source of great hilarity.

clue.text: Quietly and mutually agree over key piece of work?

parts.note: piano is the musical direction for softly
to concert is to arrange or agree jointly
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken, harmonious agreement over the central part of a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests important, but it is the keyboard: a work for the instrument with keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical composition for soloist at the keyboard with orchestra, a piece featuring keys.

clue.text: Best public act

parts.note: once news is out it is public
to do is to act

explanation.surface: The finest public performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' is a verb here, meaning to beat or surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of someone is to surpass or beat them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: 22 Face former illustrator

definitions.meaning: an old slang word for the face, short for physiognomy
pen name of Hablot Knight Browne, who drew for Dickens's novels

explanation.surface: A face drawn by an illustrator of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for one's countenance, and the pseudonym of Dickens's nineteenth-century artist.

clue.text: State of hanky panky in short ground-breaking musical

indicators.note: the slang word goes inside the shortened show title
the last letter of the show title is cut off

parts.note: Hair, the 1960s rock musical famed for breaking taboos
it is a coy slang word for sex

explanation.surface: Mischief featured in a brief, revolutionary stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean nation sharing the island of Hispaniola, an example of a sovereign country.

clue.text: Missing a hint: time to slow down

parts.note: to race less is to slow down

explanation.surface: A puzzle-solver lacking a clue is told it is time to ease off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hint' sits with 'Missing' in the definition: without a hint of something left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving no sign at all; vanished without so much as a vestige.

clue.text: To nearest and dearest it's common sense

indicators.note: these three letters are shared by both words, common to each of them

explanation.surface: Family members share ordinary good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common sense' reads as one phrase, but 'common' signals the letters shared by NEAREST and DEAREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing is one of the five senses, and the organ stands for it.

clue.text: King in area to perform, extremely unkempt and tired

indicators.note: the king letter goes inside the area word

parts.note: a zone is an area
K is the chess abbreviation for king
to do is to perform

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word unkempt

explanation.surface: A monarch in some region performs, looking scruffy and worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for exhausted or unconscious, utterly worn out.

clue.text: Value of claim ultimately getting exhaust put back

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter of the word claim
put back means the word for exhaust is reversed

parts.note: to tire is to exhaust
